hints.title: Range Pruned Subtree Search
hints.text: Utilize the BST property to prune unnecessary subtree traversals when values fall strictly outside the target range.

hints.title: BST Ordering Branch Elimination
hints.text: If the current node value is strictly less than low, any valid node must reside in its right subtree. If it exceeds high, valid nodes must be in the left subtree.

hints.title: Recursive Branch Accumulation
hints.text: Perform a recursive traversal: if node is None return 0. If node.val < low, return recurse(right). If node.val > high, return recurse(left). Otherwise return node.val + recurse(left) + recurse(right).

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: N: number of nodes in tree
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Traversing every node regardless of range wastes time exploring subtrees whose values cannot possibly match.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Pruning reduces the search space significantly, consuming only stack recursion depth proportional to tree height.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should articulate BST pruning criteria concisely rather than doing an unpruned full traversal.
complexity.notes: In a balanced BST, time is proportional to the number of nodes in the range plus the depth of boundary branches.
